value.interpretation: The same patterned bowl remains upright at the same counter location in the fixed agentview images. The current hand is visibly separated above it. The historical world +x sector is the front rim in agentview and the left rim in the CURRENT wrist view; its continuous band remains visible without an observed external obstruction. inner samples the visible inner wall in wrist view; outer samples the visible exterior in agentview. Their approximately 8 mm below-rim level, matching height, and the approximately 40 mm band span require depth verification. Neither actual opposing inner contact-face center is identifiable: the current wrist view self-occludes the centers at its lower margin, and agentview does not resolve them. Both pad measurements are unavailable. Their [0,0] pixels are schema placeholders only, not surface selections; no pad depth points are supplied. The reference polygon and region contain only visible textured bowl material away from the pinch sector. This observation does not certify unseen descent space, possession, retention, or task completion.

after_turn.interpretation: The actual frame-72 change does not expose identifiable centers of either opposing inner contact face. Agentview shows the near finger exterior; the wrist view exposes partial finger surfaces, with the centers obscured by robot self-occlusion. Neither pad has an obtainable center measurement. The schema requires pixel pairs even when visible=false; those pairs are unused and must not be sampled or interpreted as pad locations. Compared with the earlier images, the same patterned bowl remains upright on its original counter, and the hand remains visibly clear of external objects. Calibration is incomplete. The recorded execution-bound stop is not evidence of collision, and the target orientation was not achieved.

The visible proximal hand and wrist have open space for the proposed high turn, assessed separately from the finger sphere; this is not a full-arm certificate. The patterned bowl remains upright and supported on the counter, not retained by the gripper. These observations concern only the proposed high observation turn, not descent or placement. They do not certify the assumed transient displacement bound.
